notes.title: Progress Update - Summer 2025
notes.content: [p]It's been over an year since I last said anything publicly about the game, but I want to write this post to clarify that the game is still in active development more than ever.[/p][p][/p][h1]The Last Year of Development[/h1][p]A bit over one year ago the game had enemies and some environments, but honestly it wasn't good, it didn't really make sense from the perspective of game progression and narrative, it was a mess in terms of both gameplay and project management (code, assets).[/p][p]I realized that it will take more time until I have something for people to play. So in June 2024 I took a decision: to make a [b]demo [/b]for the game called [i]The Facility Project: Prologue[/i]. As the title suggests it was supposed to be a prologue, a teaser for the full game, nothing much, about 15-25 min of gameplay. Well this "demo" gave me the opportunity to remake some of the codebase and make a new level from scratch. As I worked more on the prologue, polishing everything, it was all coming together, the narrative, gameplay and progression, but it still took a lot of playtesting and listening to feedback to make it work.[/p][p]One year later this prologue turned into a game of its own. It already had over 40 minutes of gameplay, way more than I anticipated, but I did not want to remove parts of it to shorten it. I really had only 2 options: release the prologue and then work on the full game which should have at least double the duration of it OR keep the prologue as a part of the full game and build on top of it.[/p][p]Well, my decision is to NOT release the prologue as a free demo because releasing it will double or even triple the development time. I never realized what it meant to make a game with over 2 hours of gameplay, it took me almost a year to make 40 min of GOOD gameplay, so I know that the best option is to lower down the scope.[/p][p][/p][h1]The Future of Development[/h1][p]I can confidently say that I am in a much better spot than last year.[/p][p]First of all, since I polished the heck out of this prologue, I don't have to return to it. I can fully focus on making the missing part of the game (that technically has a similar structure to what I had in the previous version), unlike in the previous version where nothing was polished and I was juggling between parts of the game. Now I am developing the game chronologically, which makes much more sense.[/p][p]Secondly, the narrative and game progression is much clearer, especially thanks to Cosmin, a great game designer which helped me for almost 2 years to shape this experience.[/p][p]Third, I learned a lot, as I did from the beginning of this project. The problem was that in the previous version I used to ignore some of the issues because I had other more important things (like making the actual game work). For example, lighting and optimization, which gave me a lot of headaches and still do sometimes, but now I learned how to effectively manage both.[/p][p]Finally, I have a more active team than ever. I am still the only developer, but I collab with people on sound design, writing, voice acting, 3D art and 2D art. This just proves to me that the fact that TFP takes this long to make is a good thing in the end. How else would I form a team like this?[/p][p][/p][h1]Screenshots[/h1][p]These are some screenshots from the prologue part:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41263790/d3047aa020c567bf7beb8cd746e19e962819556f.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41263790/c5c5357d8126802e84fa6f98bb08d5b3739432d3.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41263790/bfaaaefd19483b2dd6fc58dd79032ecb4d8d06e8.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41263790/cccc0962d939e870d357909f2df57e3b2f7846d5.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Final Notes[/h1][p]In the last post I said that I can see "the light at the end of the tunnel" or something like that, anyway I kinda lied, I was just making myself feel good about the project but in reality I had only a rough idea of where it was headed. Well, whether you trust me or not, right now I confidently say that there is a plan and a finish line in sight. If we keep up the pace, we will get there, I won't say soon, but not too late either.[/p][p]Thanks to everyone who wishlisted the game! Right now we have ~1500 wishlists which is great! (I didn't really do any kind of marketing so I'm good with this number). Next announcement will probably come in the form of a trailer, but not just any trailer, a [b]release date trailer [/b](Yes an actual release date I promise).[/p][p]To keep up with updates [url="https://discord.com/invite/VfGjmGsqSn"]Join the discord server[/url] and make sure to [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1771170/The_Facility_Project/"]Wishlist the game[/url][/p]

notes.title: Creating The Perfect Game Alone - Dream or Reality?
notes.content:
[h2]Why I struggled with the development[/h2]
In this post I want to highlight something very important that persisted throughout the development of The Facility Project, my survival horror game. Since I started working on it I never had a clear picture of what the game will look at the end. This resulted in a constant change of the game: adding new levels or features and removing old stuff. 

[h2]Overthinking[/h2]
This issue was mostly caused because of overthinking, creating problems that didn't even exist. A person who thinks all the time has nothing to think about, except thoughts. That is why feedback from other people is essential. But to get the feedback you firstly need the base of the game, so that's what I started doing, building the game without complicating stuff, making everything work even if it was not perfect.

[h2]Perfectionism[/h2]
Perfection is another problem I had, since this is my first steam game it has to be perfect. But how I used this idea of perfection ruined the development. I was constantly thinking, trying to come up with the perfect design of a mechanic or level, but that's not how you find the perfect idea. To get to the idea you are looking for, you have to start creating. This way you directly get feedback from what you create and know how to improve. It's not just thoughts.

[h2]Collaboration[/h2]
In any form, anywhere, anytime, collaboration will prove to be the key to your problem. Sometimes we feel like we know better and it's our job to do it alone, we don't want to get other people involved, fearing of what they might think. In the past I made multiple smaller games in collaboration with others and they always turned out amazing. However when I decided to work on this project I wanted it to be my project, no one should help me, I wanted to prove how I can make a great game alone. I am not saying that you should never make a game alone, but if you decide to do this, you have to acknowledge that is not as easy as it seems. 

After almost 2 years I reached out to others, not directly. Some were interested and I loved to see that my game is being appreciated. I was beginning to have hope for it. That's when I started collaborating. Getting feedback, discussing ideas, creating together, this took my project to the next level. It was not just in my mind. I could express the ideas I had to others. It was a game-changer (literally).

[h2]The 2 year journey[/h2]
I learnt everything in a hard way, but very good one. The Facility Project is not just my first steam game, not just a horror game that will be forgotten after a few years when I will release much better games, it's the project that transformed me into an actual game developer. This 2 year journey was hard, on and off, either working on the game or participating in game jams, I wasn't sure if I will ever achieve what I had in mind. I lacked the confidence in my powers, knowledge and skills. I never gave up, pushed through, until I got out of the dark tunnel, until I could see the light.

[h2]Present[/h2]
Right now I am building the whole game structure, it will not be perfect at first, but after the game is playable from A to Z I can refine every little detail from the feedback I get. I am almost done with all the levels. Currently I need to finish the last 2 areas of the game.

I felt like I needed to write this out for the public, even if almost no one will read it. This will remain here forever and it will remind me if I ever find it. Thank you for reading. 

Be sure to wishlist the game and follow the game page!

notes.title: Teaser Released - Halloween 2023!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello everyone![/h3]
The Facility Project finally has a (teaser) trailer. This is not the official trailer, in the next months a gameplay trailer will be released featuring more environments, lore, creatures and mechanics! Follow the game page to stay tuned!

[h3]The Development Process[/h3]
This project has been in development for 2 years, but with huge gaps. The past 2 months I've worked really hard to bring the game to the next level. I can finally say that the whole game structure is built, but I can't reveal any release date yet. 

[h3]The Development Team[/h3]
When I started making this game I was alone. Right now I am still the only developer working in Unity game engine, but I have other people assisting me with the whole development process from sound design to game and narrative design. I assure you that we are all trying our best to nail every aspect!

[h3]Final Note[/h3]
The Facility Project is a big passion project for me and I want everyone to enjoy it and experience it like I imagined it. Thank you for having patience. I will continue to regularly post annoucements regarding the game's state!
